# @horizon-republic/nominal-types

> Runtime-validated nominal types for TypeScript. A type is a class with a rule: `new Email(text)` checks the text, so every `Email` you hold is valid, and two types never mix at compile time even when they wrap the same kind of value. Every type is a Standard Schema and a Standard JSON Schema. Optional adapters connect types to ArkType, Zod, Valibot, class-validator, NestJS, Fastify, Swagger, GraphQL, superjson, MikroORM, TypeORM, Drizzle and Sequelize.

This file describes version 3 and ships in the package: `node_modules/@horizon-republic/nominal-types/llms.txt` matches the installed code. Every docs page ships next to it under `docs/`; links are relative to this file, and the [Docs](#docs) section lists them all. Open the linked reference page for details this file leaves out.

## Rules for agents

- Input that may be wrong (requests, files, env, queue messages): `Type.parse(input)`. It returns `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, issues }` and never throws. Use `new Type(value)` only where a bad value is a bug; it throws `NominalError`.
- The functions live on the namespace `n`: `import { n } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types'`, then `n.object()`, `n.of()` and so on. They have no top-level exports. `Nominal`, the built-in types, the classes and the TypeScript types are imported by their own names.
- Declare a type as a class and put behaviour (getters, methods) in its body: `export class Sku extends AnyString.subtype('shop.Sku', /^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$/u) {}`.
- Build strings, numbers, bigints and booleans on a base type (`AnyString.subtype()`, `PositiveInteger.subtype()`). Only types under a base type have a text form, which `fromString()` and `fromEnv()` need. Use `Nominal(name, rule)` for objects and for types with no base.
- Name a type `'<part>.<Name>'`, such as `'billing.InvoiceNumber'`; each part holds letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A `/`, a space or an empty part throws `TypeError`. Built-in types are named `nominal.Email`, `nominal.Uuid` and so on. Name the class like the last part.
- Compare with `a.equals(b)`, never `===`. Read the plain value with `.value`; arithmetic needs it (`quantity.value * 2`). `>`, `<`, `Number(x)` and template strings work on the instance, except on date and time types, where `>` and `<` throw: use `Temporal.Instant.compare(a.value, b.value)`.
- Dates and times: the types from `/temporal`, never `Date` or a string type. On Node.js 22 and 24, `import 'temporal-polyfill/global'` first in the program; without `Temporal`, building a value throws `TypeError`.
- Money: `Money`. Other exact decimals: `DecimalString`. Never a `number`. Compute with `add()`, `subtract()`, `multiply()`, `compare()`; `>` and `<` on a `DecimalString` compare text.
- Ids that name their kind: `class UserId extends TypeId.subtype('shop.UserId', TypeId.withPrefix('user')) {}`, new ones with `UserId.generate()`.
- `Jwt` checks the form of a token only. Verify it with a JWT library before trusting `payload`.
- `n.matching()` takes a regular expression with no flag or only `u`; other flags throw `TypeError`. Rules must be synchronous: an asynchronous Standard Schema throws `TypeError` when a value is checked.
- Declare types holding passwords or personal data with `{ sensitive: true }`. Where messages leave the app, pass `hideValues: true` to `NominalPipe`, `fastifyNominal` or `toGraphQL()`, or call `n.hideValues(issues)`.
- A project that already uses ArkType, Zod, Valibot or class-validator keeps it and uses that adapter.
- Install an adapter's peer package yourself (`npm install zod`). Every peer is optional; nothing loads until the adapter's entry point is imported.
- Version 2.0.x code (`NType()`, `Type.getPipe()`, `FirstName`, `UUID`, constructors that checked nothing) doesn't work in version 3. Port it with [How to move from version 2](docs/guides/core/migrate-from-v2.md).

## Install and entry points

```shell
npm install @horizon-republic/nominal-types
```

Node.js 22.12 or later, ESM and CommonJS, no dependencies. The Standard Schema interfaces are exported as the types `StandardSchemaV1` and `StandardJSONSchemaV1`.

| Entry point | Exports | Peer package |

## Which tool for which job

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| one value from outside, such as a route parameter | `Uuid.parse(input)` |
| only a yes or no | `Uuid.accepts(input)`, `schema.accepts(input)` |
| a request body or a message | `n.object({ ... }).parse(body)` |
| a rule across fields | `n.constraint()` passed to `n.object()` |
| a value object of several fields | `class Stay extends Nominal('booking.Stay', n.object({ ... })) {}` |
| a PATCH body, or part of an object | `.partial()`, `.pick()`, `.omit()`, `.extend()` |
| one of several shapes told apart by a field | `n.union('method', { card: n.object(...), invoice: n.object(...) })` |
| an object whose keys are data | `n.record(CurrencyCode, DecimalString)` |
| an array of fixed positions | `n.tuple([Latitude, Longitude])` |
| a list, a missing value, `null` | `n.of(Tag).array({ max: 20 })`, `.optional()`, `.nullable()` |
| numbers or booleans from a query string or CSV | `n.of(PositiveInteger).fromString()` |
| configuration from environment variables | `n.object({ ... }).fromEnv()` |
| a fast JSON response | `schema.stringify(value)`, `Type.stringify(instance)`; `JSON.stringify(n.plain(value))` for any value |
| an existing ArkType, Zod or Valibot schema | `toArk()` + `fromArk()`, `toZod()`, `toValibot()` |
| class-validator DTOs | `@NominalField(Type)` |
| NestJS | `NominalPipe`, `NominalSerializerInterceptor`, `@NominalResponse(schema)` |
| Fastify | `fastifyNominal` with `NominalTypeProvider` |
| OpenAPI from `@nestjs/swagger` | `applyNominalTypes(document)`, `@ApiNominalBody()`, `@ApiNominalQuery()` |
| a GraphQL scalar | `toGraphQL(Type)` |
| instances through tRPC or Next.js | `superjson.registerCustom(...toSuperjson(Type))` |
| a database column | `toMikroOrm`, `toTypeOrm`, `toDrizzle`, `toSequelize` |
| any other Standard Schema library | the type itself, or `n.of(Type)` |
| test data | `arbitraryOf`, `invalidArbitraryOf`, `sampleOf` from `/testing` |

## Core API

All from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types`.

### Declare a type

- `Nominal(name, rule, options?)` returns a class to extend. `rule` is a `RegExp`, `n.matching()`, `n.satisfying()`, `n.oneOf()`, an `n.object()`, `n.union()`, `n.record()` or `n.tuple()` schema, or any synchronous Standard Schema. `NominalOptions`: `sensitive`, `implies`, `normalize` (`false` opts out of `trimStrings`).
- `Type.subtype(name, rule?, options?)` makes a narrower type. It runs the parent's rules first, and its instances pass where the parent is expected, not the other way round. A rule that narrows the value (`n.oneOf()`) narrows the type of `value` too.
- `Type.variant(name, rule, options?)` makes a sibling: the same methods, its own rule in place of the source's, and the two don't mix.
- `implies: [OtherType]` says every value also passes `OtherType`, so instances pass for it at compile time, for `instanceof` and for `equals()`. It is trusted, not checked.
- `n.matching(pattern, description?, json?)` returns a `PatternSchema`. `description` completes "must be …"; `json` adds JSON Schema keywords.
- `n.satisfying(guard, description, json?)` returns a `PredicateSchema` from a type guard. Without `json` the type has no JSON Schema.
- `n.oneOf(...values)` returns a `OneOfSchema` for a fixed set of strings, finite numbers, booleans or `null` (`OneOfValue`). It takes no enum object: spread `Object.values()` of a string enum.
- `n.isType(value)` tells whether a value is a nominal type class, also from another copy of the package.

```ts
import { AnyString, n, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export class Sku extends AnyString.subtype('shop.Sku', n.matching(/^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$/u, 'a SKU', { examples: ['TEA-0042'] })) {
  public get category(): string {
    return this.value.slice(0, 3);
  }
}

export class Quantity extends PositiveInteger.subtype(
  'shop.Quantity',
  n.satisfying((value: unknown): value is number => typeof value === 'number' && value <= 99, 'at most 99', { maximum: 99 }),
) {}

export class Password extends AnyString.subtype('shop.Password', /^.{12,}$/u, { sensitive: true }) {}

export class OrderStatus extends AnyString.subtype('shop.OrderStatus', n.oneOf('draft', 'paid', 'shipped')) {}

new Sku('TEA-0042').category; // 'TEA'
Quantity.parse(100); // { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must be at most 99 (was 100)' }] }
Password.parse('short'); // issue message 'must be matched by ^.{12,}$ (was a string of 5 characters)'
new OrderStatus('paid').value; // 'paid', typed 'draft' | 'paid' | 'shipped'
```

Details: [Declaring types](docs/reference/declaring.md).

### Members of a type

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `new Type(input)` | checks and returns an instance; throws `NominalError` |
| `Type.parse(input)` | `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, issues }`; never throws |
| `Type.parseAsync(input)` | a Promise of the instance, rejected with `NominalError`; for libraries that await a throwing parser (tRPC) |
| `Type.accepts(input)` | `true` when `parse()` would succeed, without building an instance |
| `Type.stringify(instance)` | the JSON text, faster than `JSON.stringify()` |
| `value instanceof Type` | `true` for its and its subtypes' instances, across copies of the package; reads the brand only, so use `parse()` to know a value is valid |
| `Type.typeName`, `Type.rule`, `Type['~standard']` | the name, the rule of its own level, the Standard Schema interface |
| `instance.value` | the checked value; `readonly`; an object value is frozen |
| `instance.equals(other)` | same type line and same value; deep for objects |
| `instance.toJSON()`, `toString()` | the value; big integers as a decimal string, dates and times as their text |
| getters per field, `copyWith(changes)` | on `n.object()` types; `copyWith` returns a checked copy or throws `NominalError` |

`parse()` returns an instance of the same type or a subtype as it is. Any other instance (a parent, a variant, another copy, a forged object) is checked again; an unrelated type is refused. Methods that return a changed copy (`canonical()`, `withTag()`) keep the class of `this`. An `n.object()` field can't be named `value`, `equals`, `copyWith`, `toJSON`, `toString` or `constructor`. Details: [Type members](docs/reference/type-members.md).

### Schemas

Every schema has `.parse()`, `.parseAsync()`, `.accepts()`, `.toPlain(value)` (instances replaced by `toJSON()`, declared fields only) and `.stringify(value)` (the JSON text of `toPlain()`, generated per schema). Every chained call returns a new schema.

- `n.of(Type)` returns a `TypeSchema`. Chain `.array(options?)` (`ArrayOptions`: `length`, `min`, `max`, `unique`), `.optional()`, `.nullable()`, `.fromString()` (only right after `n.of()`, for a type with a text form).
- `n.object(fields, ...constraints)` returns an `ObjectSchema`. A field is a type, a schema or any Standard Schema; a field that accepts `undefined` may be missing, any other reads `is required`. Undeclared keys are dropped; `.strict()` refuses them. `.fromEnv()` reads fields from text and hides values in messages. `.partial()`, `.required()`, `.pick()`, `.omit()`, `.extend()`, `.keys`.
- `n.union(key, { tag: n.object(...) })` returns a `UnionSchema`: the input's `key` picks the variant. The value type narrows on `value[key]`.
- `n.record(Key, Value)` returns a `RecordSchema`. `Key` is a type or schema of strings; `n.oneOf()` keys are all required (`.partial()` frees them). `.min(n)`, `.max(n)` count keys.
- `n.tuple([A, B], Rest?)` returns a `TupleSchema`; trailing optional positions may be left out.
- `n.constraint(fields, check, options?)` returns a `Constraint`, a rule across fields like a SQL `CHECK`. `check` gets the checked values and returns `true`, `false` or a message; `ConstraintOptions`: `path`, `message`. It runs once every field is valid.
- `n.plain(value)` copies any value with every instance replaced by its `toJSON()` (`Plain<Value>`). Use it before `JSON.stringify()` on large responses.
- `n.isObject(value)`, `n.isConstraint(value)` tell schemas and constraints apart.

```ts
import { AnyString, CurrencyCode, DecimalString, Email, Latitude, Longitude, n, Nominal, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

const withinCapacity = n.constraint(
  { guests: PositiveInteger, capacity: PositiveInteger },
  ({ guests, capacity }) => guests <= capacity || 'must not exceed the capacity',
  { path: 'guests' },
);

export const CreateBooking = n.object(
  { customer: Email, guests: PositiveInteger, capacity: PositiveInteger, note: n.of(AnyString).optional() },
  withinCapacity,
);

CreateBooking.parse({ customer: 'jane@example.com', guests: 3, capacity: 2 });
// { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must not exceed the capacity', path: ['guests'] }] }

export class Stay extends Nominal('booking.Stay', n.object({ guests: PositiveInteger, capacity: PositiveInteger }, withinCapacity)) {
  public get free(): number {
    return this.capacity.value - this.guests.value;
  }
}

new Stay({ guests: 2, capacity: 3 }).free; // 1
new Stay({ guests: 2, capacity: 3 }).copyWith({ guests: 5 }); // throws NominalError: booking.Stay: guests: must not exceed the capacity

export const Payment = n.union('method', {
  card: n.object({ last4: n.matching(/^\d{4}$/u) }),
  invoice: n.object({ email: Email }),
});

export const Prices = n.record(CurrencyCode, DecimalString).max(50);
export const Point = n.tuple([Latitude, Longitude]);
```

Configuration from the environment:

```ts
import { AnyBoolean, n, Nominal, PositiveInteger, Url } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export class Config extends Nominal('app.Config', n.object({ PORT: PositiveInteger, DEBUG: n.of(AnyBoolean).optional(), DATABASE_URL: Url }).fromEnv()) {}

const config = new Config(process.env); // throws one NominalError listing every bad variable
config.PORT.value; // 3000 for PORT=3000
```

Details: [Schemas](docs/reference/schemas.md).

### Errors and messages

- `NominalError` extends `TypeError`, with `typeName`, `issues` (`{ message, path? }[]`) and `message` such as `'nominal.Uuid: must be a UUID (was "x")'`.
- Messages read `must be <description> (was <value>)`. A sensitive type writes the value by kind only: `(was a string of 7 characters)`. `Email`, `E164PhoneNumber`, `IpAddress` and the types under it, `MacAddress`, `Iban` and `Jwt` are sensitive.
- `n.hideValues(issues)` hides the value in each message the same way.
- Rules from other libraries keep their own messages.

Details: [Errors and messages](docs/reference/errors-and-messages.md).

### n.configure()

`n.configure(options)` sets process-wide settings shared by every copy of the package. Call it once, in a module the entry point imports first. It returns the previous settings (`FullConfiguration`), and throws `TypeError` on an unknown option, changing nothing. `Configuration` options:

- `messages`: a `MessageFunction`, which takes an `IssueDetails` and returns a string or `undefined`, or a `MessageMap` by `IssueCode`, to translate messages (`Messages` is either).
- `values`: `'show'` (default), `'length'` or `'hide'` for the value in messages.
- `inspect`: `'hide'` hides every value from `console.log()`.
- `codes`: `true` adds `code: IssueCode` to every issue (`NominalIssue`).
- `normalize: { trimStrings: true }`: types under `AnyString` trim input first.
- `codegen`: `'off'` never calls `new Function`, for a CSP without `'unsafe-eval'`.

```ts
import { n } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

n.configure({ codes: true, values: 'length', messages: { required: 'ist erforderlich' } });
```

Details: [n.configure()](docs/reference/configure.md).

### JSON Schema

`Type['~standard'].jsonSchema.input({ target })` and `.output({ target })`, with `target` one of `'draft-2020-12'`, `'draft-07'`, `'openapi-3.0'`. `title` is the type name. A rule without JSON Schema (`n.satisfying()` without `json`) throws `TypeError`. Details: [JSON Schema](docs/reference/json-schema.md).

### TypeScript types

`ValueOf<Schema>` gives a schema's value type (`type CreateBookingBody = ValueOf<typeof CreateBooking>`; give it its own name, not the schema's). `StandardOf<typeof MyType>` types `~standard` of a class with members of its own: `declare static readonly '~standard': StandardOf<typeof MyType>;`. The others: `InputOf`, `Parsed`, `NominalType`, `NominalInstance`, `AnyNominalType`, `NominalSchema`, `SubtypeOf`, `SubtypeInstance`, `ImplyingType`, `Narrowed`, `VariantOf`, `VariantInstance`, `Brand`, `Branded`, `BrandsOf`, `Unbranded`, `Immutable`, `ObjectInstance`, `ObjectCopy`, `ObjectRule`, `ObjectFields`, `ObjectInput`, `ObjectValue`, `TextInput`, `UnionInput`, `UnionValue`, `UnionVariants`, `RecordKey`, `RecordInput`, `RecordValue`, `TupleValue`, `NominalTarget`, `TargetValue`, `AnyConstraint`, `ConstraintField`, `ConstraintInput`, `ConstraintInputs`, `ConstraintValue`, `ConstraintValues`, `ConstraintVerdict`, `StandardProps`, `StandardSchema`. Details: [TypeScript types](docs/reference/typescript-types.md).

## Built-in types

Each is named `nominal.<Class>` and has a text form, except `Money`. "Under X" means a subtype of X. Methods listed are the main ones; the reference pages list all.

Strings ([Strings](docs/reference/types/string.md)):

- `AnyString`: any string. `NonEmptyString`: not `''`. `NonBlankString`: under `NonEmptyString`, not only white space.
- `Email`: an RFC 5322 dot-atom address up to 254 characters; sensitive; `local`, `domain`, `tag`, `withTag()`, `canonical()`, `isSameMailbox()`.
- `E164PhoneNumber`: `+` and up to 15 digits with an assigned country code, no spaces or dashes; format only; sensitive; `countryCallingCode`, `nationalNumber`.
- `Uuid`: any case, `equals` ignores case; `version`, `timestamp`, `canonical()`. `UuidV4`, `UuidV7`: under `Uuid`, that version.
- `Ulid`: 26 Crockford base32 characters; `timestamp`. `ObjectId`: 24 hex digits; `timestamp`.
- `TypeId`: `prefix_suffix` (spec v0.3.0); `prefix`, `toUuid()`, static `withPrefix(prefix)`, `generate(prefix?)`, `fromUuid()`.
- `SemVer`: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, no `v`; `major`, `minor`, `patch`, `compare()`, `isNewerThan()`.
- `Url`: an absolute URL of any scheme, `javascript:` included; `toURL()`. `HttpUrl`: http or https only; use it for links.
- `Hostname`: RFC 1123; `isSubdomainOf()`, `toUnicode()`. `DomainName`: under `Hostname`, two labels or more.
- `IpAddress`: IPv4 or IPv6 text; sensitive; `version`, `isPrivate`, `isLoopback`, `canonical()`. `Ipv4Address`, `Ipv6Address`: under `IpAddress`.
- `IpPrefix`: CIDR with host bits zero; `contains()`. `Ipv4Prefix`, `Ipv6Prefix`: under `IpPrefix`.
- `MacAddress`: EUI-48, `:` or `-`; sensitive.
- `CountryCode`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, plus `XK`; `flag`. `CurrencyCode`: ISO 4217 upper case; `minorUnits`.
- `LanguageTag`: BCP 47; `language`, `region`. `MediaType`: `type/subtype` with parameters; `essence`, `isJson`.
- `DecimalString`: an exact decimal as text (`'1.50'`; `+`, `.5`, `1e3` refused); `add()`, `subtract()`, `multiply()`, `compare()`, `toMinorUnits()`.
- `HexColor`: `#` and 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex digits; `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`.
- `Base64`: RFC 4648 §4 with padding; `toBytes()`. `Base64Url`: §5 without padding, a sibling of `Base64`.
- `Jwt`: a compact JWS token, form only, never verified; sensitive; `header`, `payload`, `expiresAt`.
- `Isbn` (10 or 13 digits, no hyphens), `Issn` (`NNNN-NNNC`), `Gtin` (8, 12, 13, 14 digits), `Isin`: check digits checked at runtime only.
- `Iban`: electronic form, no spaces, country length and MOD 97 checked; sensitive; `toPrint()`. `Bic`: ISO 9362, 8 or 11 characters.

Numbers ([Numbers](docs/reference/types/number.md)): none converts text; `PositiveInteger.parse('2')` fails, `n.of(PositiveInteger).fromString()` reads it.

- `AnyNumber`: any number. `FiniteNumber`: finite. `PositiveNumber`, `NegativeNumber`, `NonNegativeNumber`, `NonPositiveNumber`: finite, `> 0`, `< 0`, `≥ 0`, `≤ 0`. `Float32`: a 32-bit float.
- `Latitude`, `Longitude`: under `FiniteNumber`, -90 to 90 and -180 to 180.
- `Integer`: a safe integer. `PositiveInteger`, `NegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonPositiveInteger`: `≥ 1`, `≤ -1`, `≥ 0`, `≤ 0`.
- `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Uint8`, `Uint16`, `Uint32`: sized integers. `Port`: under `Uint16`, 1 to 65535.

Big integers ([Big integers](docs/reference/types/bigint.md)): `value` is a `bigint`; input is a bigint, a decimal string or a safe integer; `toJSON()` writes a decimal string.

- `AnyBigInt`. `PositiveBigInt`, `NegativeBigInt`, `NonNegativeBigInt`, `NonPositiveBigInt`. `Int64`, `Uint64`.

Others:

- `AnyBoolean` ([Booleans](docs/reference/types/boolean.md)): `true` or `false`; from text only `'true'` and `'false'`.
- `Money` ([Money](docs/reference/types/money.md)): `{ amount: DecimalString, currency: CurrencyCode }`, JSON `{ "amount": "12.34", "currency": "EUR" }`, no more digits than the currency's minor units; `add`, `subtract`, `multiply(integer)`, `compare` (`TypeError` across currencies), `minor`, static `fromMinor()`, `format()`.

Implied types: a narrower number type passes for the wider ones its values always fit (`PositiveInteger` for `NonNegativeInteger`, `Uint8` for `Int16`), and every string type that refuses `''` passes for `NonEmptyString` and `NonBlankString`. The lists are in the reference pages.

Dates and times, from `/temporal` ([Dates and times](docs/reference/types/temporal.md)). `value` is the Temporal object; input is strict RFC 3339 text or a Temporal object of the kind.

- `Instant`: `2024-05-01T09:30:00Z` or with an offset; `toJSON()` writes UTC; `toDate()`.
- `PlainDate`: `2024-05-01`. `PlainTime`: `09:30:00` or `09:30`. `PlainDateTime`: `2024-05-01T09:30:00`.
- `ZonedDateTime`: `2024-05-01T09:30:00+02:00[Europe/Paris]`, the offset must match the zone; `timeZone`, `toInstant()`.
- `Duration`: `P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S`, no sign; `equals` unit by unit.
- `TimeZoneId`: an IANA zone name the runtime knows; under `AnyString`.

```ts
import 'temporal-polyfill/global';
import { Instant } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/temporal';

const sent = new Instant('2024-05-01T11:30:00+02:00');

sent.toJSON(); // '2024-05-01T09:30:00Z'
Temporal.Instant.compare(sent.value, new Instant('2024-05-01T10:00:00Z').value); // -1
Instant.parse('2024-05-01 09:30:00').ok; // false
```

## Adapters

One page per entry point: [Adapters](docs/reference/adapters/README.md).

### ArkType

```ts
import { type } from 'arktype';
import { Email, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import { fromArk, toArk } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/arktype';

export const CreateOrder = fromArk(type({ customer: toArk(Email), quantity: toArk(PositiveInteger), 'note?': 'string' }));

CreateOrder.parse({ customer: 'jane@example.com', quantity: 2 }); // { ok: true, value: { customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger } }
```

`toArk(Type)` is a field; `fromArk(type, ...constraints)` returns an `ArkSchema` that gives instances. `constrainArk(objectType, ...constraints)` adds constraints to a nested object.

### Zod and Valibot

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';
import * as v from 'valibot';
import { Email, n, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import { constrainZod, toZod } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/zod';
import { toValibot } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/valibot';

const quantityAtMost99 = n.constraint({ quantity: PositiveInteger }, ({ quantity }) => quantity.value <= 99 || 'must be at most 99');

export const CreateOrder = constrainZod(z.object({ customer: toZod(Email), quantity: toZod(PositiveInteger) }), quantityAtMost99);

CreateOrder.safeParse({ customer: 'jane@example.com', quantity: 2 }); // { success: true, data: { customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger } }

export const Contact = v.object({ email: toValibot(Email) });
```

`constrainValibot(object, ...constraints)` does the same for Valibot. Zod's `parse()` throws `ZodError` and Valibot's `v.parse()` throws `ValiError`; use `safeParse()`.

### class-validator

```ts
import { Email, n, Uuid } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import { NominalField } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/class-validator';

export class CreateOrderDto {
  @NominalField(Email)
  public customer!: Email;

  @NominalField(n.of(Uuid).array({ min: 1, max: 50 }))
  public items!: readonly Uuid[];
}
```

`@NominalField(target, options?)` checks the property and turns it into instances under `plainToInstance`.

### NestJS

```ts
import { Body, Controller, Get, Param, Post, Query } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Email, n, PositiveInteger, Uuid } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import type { ValueOf } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import { NominalPipe, NominalResponse } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/nest';

const CreateOrder = n.object({ customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger });
type CreateOrderBody = ValueOf<typeof CreateOrder>;

@Controller('orders')
export class OrdersController {
  @Get(':id')
  public find(@Param('id') id: Uuid): void {} // checked by the global pipe from the declared type

  @Get()
  public list(@Query('ids', new NominalPipe(n.of(Uuid).array({ max: 100 }))) ids: readonly Uuid[]): void {}

  @Post()
  @NominalResponse(CreateOrder)
  public create(@Body(new NominalPipe(CreateOrder)) order: CreateOrderBody): CreateOrderBody {
    return order;
  }
}

// main.ts: app.useGlobalPipes(new NominalPipe());
```

- `new NominalPipe(target?, options?)`: without a target it checks parameters whose declared type is a nominal type. Declared types lose array items and `?`, so give a list or an optional value its own pipe. Options: `fromString`, `hideValues`, `exceptionFactory` (default `BadRequestException`).
- Give a schema's value type its own name (`CreateOrderBody`); a type alias named like the schema breaks Swagger and pipes under Bun and SWC.
- Responses: Nest's `ClassSerializerInterceptor` writes instances as `{ "value": … }`. Use `NominalSerializerInterceptor` in its place (same arguments), or `@NominalResponse(schema)` (`NominalResponseInterceptor`) to write with `schema.stringify()`. A Fastify response schema mishandles instances; return `schema.toPlain(value)` or use one of these.

### Fastify

```ts
import Fastify from 'fastify';
import { Email, n, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import { fastifyNominal } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/fastify';
import type { NominalTypeProvider } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/fastify';

const CreateOrder = n.object({ customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger });

const app = Fastify().withTypeProvider<NominalTypeProvider>();

await app.register(fastifyNominal);

app.post('/orders', { schema: { body: CreateOrder } }, (request) => ({ domain: request.body.customer.domain }));
```

Nominal schemas work in `body`, `querystring`, `params`, `headers` and `response`; other JSON Schemas still go to Ajv. Options: `fromString`, `hideValues`, `jsonSchemaTarget`. `nominalValidatorCompiler()` and `nominalSerializerCompiler()` serve routes whose every schema is nominal.

### Other frameworks

- tRPC: `.input(schema)` as it is; bad input fails with `BAD_REQUEST` and a `NominalError` as `cause`.
- Hono `sValidator('json', schema)`, Elysia `{ body: schema }`, React Hook Form `standardSchemaResolver(schema)`: as they are; text fields need `n.of(Type).fromString()`.
- TanStack Form: validate with `schema['~standard'].validate(value)` in a function.
- Next.js: `Schema.parse(Object.fromEntries(formData))`, `Schema.parse(await request.json())`.

### Swagger

- `applyNominalTypes(document)` on the result of `SwaggerModule.createDocument()` fills the schemas of nominal types (`OpenApiDocument`).
- `@ApiNominalProperty(target, options?)` on a DTO property; `@ApiNominalBody(target, options?)` and `@ApiNominalQuery(name, target, options?)` on a route that checks with `NominalPipe` (`ApiNominalBodyOptions`, `ApiNominalQueryOptions`).
- A minified server build must keep class names (esbuild `keepNames: true`).

### GraphQL and superjson

- `toGraphQL(Type, options?)` returns a `GraphQLScalarType` named like the last part of the type name (`GraphQLOptions`: `name`, `description`, `hideValues`, …).
- `superjson.registerCustom(...toSuperjson(Email))` keeps instances across tRPC and Next.js. Register each type, subtypes too, on both sides.

### Databases

| ORM | Use |
| --- | --- |
| MikroORM 7 | `p.type(toMikroOrm(Email))` in `defineEntity`, or `@Property({ type: toMikroOrm(Email) })` |
| TypeORM | `@Column(toTypeOrm(Email, { nullable: true }))` |
| Drizzle | `const email = customType<DrizzleColumn<typeof Email>>(toDrizzle(Email));`, then `email('email')` |
| Sequelize 6 | `email: toSequelize(Email)` as a model attribute |

The column type follows the type (`Email` `varchar(254)`, `Uuid` `uuid`, `DecimalString` `numeric`, `Instant` `timestamptz`, objects JSON); see [Database columns](docs/reference/adapters/database-columns.md). Reads are checked and throw `NominalError` for a stored value the type refuses; `trusted: true` skips the check. A `DecimalString` read as a JS number throws, so keep the column exact.

## Testing

```ts
import fc from 'fast-check';
import { Email, n, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import { arbitraryOf, invalidArbitraryOf, sampleOf } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/testing';

const CreateOrder = n.object({ customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger });

fc.assert(fc.property(arbitraryOf(CreateOrder), (body) => CreateOrder.parse(body).ok));
fc.assert(fc.property(arbitraryOf(CreateOrder, { as: 'instances' }), (order) => order.quantity.value > 0));
fc.assert(fc.property(invalidArbitraryOf(Email), (value) => !Email.parse(value).ok));
sampleOf(Email, 3, { seed: 42 }); // three valid addresses, the same on every run
```

A target is a type or an `n.of()`, `n.object()`, `n.record()`, `n.tuple()` or `n.union()` schema. A type of your own with only a type guard needs `overrides: new Map([[Type, fc.constantFrom(...)]])`. Details: [Testing](docs/reference/testing.md).
